literature.title: Efficient Reasoning with Balanced Thinking
literature.authors: Yulin Li, Tengyao Tu, Li Ding, Junjie Wang, Huiling Zhen, Yixin Chen, Yong Li, Zhuotao Tian
literature.evidence: Paper confidence is geometric mean of tokenwise maximum probabilities. Its projection explanation uses the unit mean-difference direction. The current project instead follows the public mixed lexical/low-confidence labels, raw vector, arithmetic confidence and diagonal-LDA-derived displacement coefficients. Table 3 reports worse 1.5B MATH results with longer windows; it is contrary evidence to unconditional smoothing.
literature.implication: Candidate A is our constrained Euclidean geometry derivation using the current fitted readout, not a paper method or a reproduction. Correlation/decodability and smaller norm do not prove causal usefulness.
literature.reading: Entire parsed main text, references and appendices read; crucial ReBalance and Reflection equations also visually inspected.

literature.title: EasySteer: A Unified Framework for High-Performance and Extensible LLM Steering
literature.authors: Haolei Xu, Xinyu Mei, Yuchen Yan, Rui Zhou, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen
literature.evidence: Exposes vector extraction and per-layer additive steering within the inference engine. This makes a fixed-layer vector replacement feasible without altering model weights. Reported framework overhead is not a guarantee for this project controller or a shorter-token run.
literature.implication: Keep algorithm, runtime, layer and all dynamic coefficients unchanged while replacing the vector through the existing from_pt_direction payload.
literature.reading: Entire parsed main text, references and appendices read; crucial ReBalance and Reflection equations also visually inspected.

literature.title: Adaptive Activation Steering for Efficient LLM Reasoning via Closed-Loop PID Control
locators: Section 3 redundancy classifier and PID loop
literature.evidence: Uses short hidden-state chunks and a learned redundancy signal, with PID strengths and temperature adaptation. Its small evaluation and coupled temperature change do not isolate the benefit of smoother control.
literature.implication: Do not import PID gains or temperature changes as an established optimization. Candidate C tests one confidence-estimation mechanism on CPU first.
literature.reading: Entire parsed main text, references and appendices read; crucial ReBalance and Reflection equations also visually inspected.

literature.title: Reflection Steering: Disentangling Reflection from Reasoning in Activation Space for Token-Efficient Inference
literature.authors: Hu Jiarui, Zhiyuan Wen, Xiaoyun Liu, Jiaxing Shen, Yu Yang
locators: Evaluation protocol and independent training-set pilot
literature.evidence: Uses labeled full spans, centered PCA, orthogonalization against the pooled activation mean, multilayer selection and bounded projection removal. The pooled mean is explicitly a rank-one proxy, not a complete general-reasoning subspace. Its independent pilot did not establish the stated 1 percentage point accuracy-equivalence margin.
literature.implication: Candidate B isolates only pooled-mean removal and preserves our existing readout displacement; it is not a full reproduction. It uses our step-start states and unchanged labels, with no layer/rank/strength search. A local norm bound does not control downstream amplification.
literature.reading: Entire parsed main text, references and appendices read; crucial ReBalance and Reflection equations also visually inspected.

literature.title: When Does Learning to Stop Help? A Cost-Aware Study of Early Exits in Reasoning Models
literature.authors: Zhe Dong, Fang Qin, Manish Shah
literature.status: arXiv preprint; PDF cover also displays July 7, 2026
literature.evidence: Uses forced short answers at checkpoints and prefix-observable confidence/agreement features. Probe decoding and repeated prefix prefill can change the cost conclusion. Its 15% risk allowance is not an accuracy-preservation target for this project.
literature.implication: Candidate D needs checkpoint answer labels and a tested KV fork preserving dynamic state; ordinary final-answer occurrences are insufficient. Current integration has checkpointing and eviction replay, not a verified forked-probe path. Defer this larger implementation from the vector batch.
literature.code_read: gen() tokenizes each input and invokes model.generate; inspected code does not demonstrate the paper cost model of reusable KV forks.
literature.reading: Entire parsed main text, references and appendices read; crucial ReBalance and Reflection equations also visually inspected.

plan.purpose: The original half-step proxy passed, but this can reflect generic shrinkage rather than useful previous-step information. One additional CPU diagnostic distinguishes these mechanisms before paying for a controller implementation.
plan.data: Same 400/100 calibration development groups; no new independent evidence and no benchmark answers.
plan.fixed_control: Estimate one probability mean from all complete-step tokens in the 400 training questions. At each evaluated half-step use exactly the same previous-token count (min(previous complete step length,8)), but replace their probabilities with that fixed mean. The same current first-half tokens and second-half target are retained.
plan.primary: Equal-question MSE on steps of 2..8 tokens in the 100 calibration validation questions.
plan.advance_only_if: Previous-step pooling MSE is at least 5% lower than this fixed training-mean shrinkage control. Otherwise the claimed temporal-information advantage is unsupported and the temporal candidate is deferred without a GPU test or threshold search.
plan.interpretation: This new specificity gate is explicitly a follow-up to the first CPU diagnostic, not a retrospectively claimed preregistration. Neither result estimates generated accuracy or compression.

gpu_plan.advance_rule: At least 5% lower mean thinking AND total tokens, correct count no lower, cap count no higher. These are exploratory screen criteria; no claim of established accuracy preservation.
gpu_plan.estimate_basis: Previous fresh 1.5B training groups of 100 used about 127-155 seconds each; new difficulty/caps and hardware can differ. Total estimate includes startup/checks with margin, not a guaranteed upper runtime.
gpu_plan.cost: Pre-run estimate only: hourly price times 0.25-0.42 hours. Actual hourly price and billed uptime remain unknown.
gpu_plan.stop: Stop on mismatch/OOM/numerical error/incomplete group; group timeout 600 seconds (including evaluation-loop grading), batch wall limit 1800 seconds. Preserve partials; no retry or 7B/full-test expansion.
gpu_plan.authorization: User supplied SSH in direct response to the fixed 3x100 batch/start request; GPU mode independently verified active and idle before execution. Scope consumed once; no reserve or further GPU authorization.
gpu_plan.completion: All 300 answers complete and paired; CPU author grades and requested metrics saved with hashes. Notify GPU may be shut down immediately after generation processes exit; transfer and hash outputs before server shutdown.

limitations: CPU geometry and prediction errors are not actual CoT compression or accuracy measurements.
The calibration validation fold has prior layer-selection exposure and is development evidence.
Both vector candidates preserve a noisy calibration readout displacement, not semantic truth.
A and B are independent single-factor alternatives, never combined in this screen.
Screening two candidates uses shared development validation; choose at most one with the fixed rule before separately authorized independent confirmation.
A 100-question result cannot certify a 1 percentage point accuracy-loss bound.
Frozen baseline outputs/tag and the two finished negative experiments remain unchanged.
Observed token reductions of 1.51% and 3.42% and correct-count gains do not satisfy the pre-fixed joint advancement rule; they are not zero effects, nor confirmed population benefits.
Author grades are the reporting standard. Math-verify correct totals are 80/84/81 and have item-level disagreements even when group totals agree; no regrading or score edits were performed.
Two candidates share this 100-question screening set. The disjoint 200-question confirmation set was not generated, and no accuracy preservation claim is established.
No actual preemptions occurred in the three groups, so this run does not newly validate state restoration under preemption.
